roleInterpretation: Own V-V8 Lighting: authored illumination and visibility conditions that preserve the Veilwild visual grammar while making concealment/search readable but non-trivial. Lighting is producer-owned here; camouflage semantics remain A12, environment source remains A05, visual thesis remains A04, and final rendering/integration/performance/judgment remain with their respective owners.
topFalsifiers: The exact baseline contains campaign topology/protocol material but no Veilwild Godot runtime scene or authored lighting artifact to demonstrate V-V8 in-product consequence.
An editor-preview sun/environment could appear acceptable yet disappear at runtime unless an explicit DirectionalLight3D and WorldEnvironment are part of the real project.
Lighting can accidentally collapse concealment into either near-invisibility or trivial silhouette/readability, violating the V-V8 oracle while still looking aesthetically coherent.
Camera-level Environment overrides, exposure/tonemapping, material response, or A12 camouflage shader behavior can invalidate a fixture-tuned lighting condition after integration.
Directional shadow range/splits, soft-shadow settings or GI/post-processing can create shadow instability or material frame cost that only appears in the real encounter camera/performance condition.

Runtime Workspace admission reports the exact requested commit and clean detached state but a sourceStateDigest different from the campaign-supplied digest; digest semantics must be revalidated before using the runtime digest as campaign identity proof.
expectedInputs: A04/F04 visual-development contract: palette, mood, readability hierarchy, target time/weather grammar and acceptable contrast range.
A05/F05 environment authoritative scene/interchange plus intended search paths, canopy/occluder structure and concealment contexts.
A10/F10 material/lookdev contract: environment and creature material response assumptions relevant to illumination.
A12/F12 camouflage/rendering interface requirements once available, especially state/environment parameters whose visual consequence lighting must preserve.
A17/F17 real Godot project/runtime integration point and renderer/camera environment conventions.
A20/F21 exact performance condition/budget when the integrated candidate is available.
expectedOutputs: F11 lighting/visibility interface contract with Godot carrier, explicit light/environment parameters, preconditions and consumer-visible failure modes.
An authored reusable Godot lighting resource/scene or integration-ready fixture that can be replayed against the real environment rather than editor preview lighting.
Mechanical validation that explicit runtime lighting exists and is stable under a declared camera/renderer condition; visual captures may be evidence but not Human detectability proof.
Owner-correct repair receipts for lighting-specific defects and a bounded statement of what remains dependent on A04/A05/A10/A12/A17/A20 inputs.
highestRiskBoundaryAssumption: A lighting rig can be authored independently enough to create useful product pressure without silently choosing A04 visual semantics or A12 camouflage semantics; therefore any pre-integration lighting artifact must remain explicitly provisional until replayed on the real environment/material/camera/camouflage condition.
